**SECTION C: COMPREHENSION (10 MARKS)**

Read the following passage then answer the questions that follow. Be concise and use your own words.

**Malaria**

Malaria is an infectious disease transmitted by mosquitoes. Worldwide, malaria affects between 300 and 500 million people each year. About 1,000 cases of malaria occur each year in the United States. Thousands of people die every day from malaria in Africa. Many tourists coming to Africa are warned in advance of this deadly disease so that they can take anti-malaria treatment before they make their journey. Malaria is treatable and should be taken very seriously. If left untreated, the infected person can develop infection in the brain, so-called cerebral malaria, and end up with fever and coma.

Malaria is also called biduotertian fever, blackwater fever, falciparum malaria, plasmodium, quartan malaria or tertian malaria. There are many symptoms of malaria and not every individual experiences all the symptoms. The symptoms are divided into three distinct stages.

- The first stage is called the cold stage. Symptoms of this stage are sudden chills, and sometimes violent shaking.
- The second stage is called the hot stage. This stage is characterised by a high fever and rapid breathing. The fever may reach 107° F.
- The third stage is called the wet stage. This stage is characterised by excessive sweating.

Malaria kills about three times as many Africans each year as does AIDS, and it is one of the top two killers of African children. Yet unlike AIDS, malaria is largely treatable. So why are more Africans dying from it?

The disease was largely wiped out by the lavish use of the insecticide known as DDT in many European and American countries in the 1950s. It was mistakenly thought to have been brought under control in the poorer countries by the drug Chloroquine. Today, malaria is spreading at an alarming rate.

There are several reasons why malaria is on the increase again. This parasite keeps on developing resistance to medicines like Chloroquine, designed to combat the disease and used as a curative or preventive drug in the 1970s. One reason why the parasite becomes resistant is that it is very adaptable. There are many different forms of it, and if one form has a natural resistance to a particular drug, it will survive and then increase in number. Another reason is that some malaria sufferers do not treat the disease properly: they may not have enough money to pay for the full treatment; they may not know which quantity of the drug to take and how; they may buy diluted drugs. In such cases, the parasite may become more resistant and harder to treat in the future. In the past, whenever a parasite became resistant to a drug, a new one was often becoming available to fight it; but now there is less interest in Europe and America in producing new drugs, as there is for AIDS: malaria does not come as a sudden epidemic, it is a slow but sure killer. Because it is not dramatic and does not appear on TV screens, less attention is given to it.

Hopes that the disease could be eradicated by such measures as spraying houses with DDT or draining stagnant water have faded with the growing power of organisations concerned with protecting the environment. They argue that those methods harm the environment.

Health workers now focus more on protecting people, less on destroying mosquitoes. While waiting for a vaccine to be found, African health workers are going back to some old-fashioned methods, like the use of mosquito nets dipped in an insecticide solution, which can repel mosquitoes for up to six months.

*(Culled from the internet, February 2008.)*

**QUESTIONS**

1) Choose the correct answer and write in the space provided. According to the text, malaria kills: a) as much as AIDS does; b) more than AIDS; c) three times each year; d) less than AIDS does. (1 mark)

2) Give two main reasons why malaria becomes resistant to some drugs. (2 marks)

3) According to the text, give two reasons why the western countries are no longer interested in malaria. (2 marks)

4) What two differences does the author make in the text between malaria and AIDS? (2 marks)

5) Why did the authorities stop the use of DDT to eradicate malaria? (2 marks)

6) Give the synonym of "wiped out." (1 mark)

**Question concernée : n°1 (1 mark).**

### Rappel de méthode
Une question de compréhension se répond en reformulant un passage précis du texte. Quand une question demande un nombre précis de raisons ou de différences, il faut les distinguer clairement l'une de l'autre plutôt que de développer une seule idée sous deux formulations proches.

**Réponse : b) more than AIDS.**

Le texte indique explicitement que le paludisme tue environ trois fois plus d'Africains chaque année que le sida (« Malaria kills about three times as many Africans each year as does AIDS ») : « more than AIDS » restitue fidèlement cette affirmation, contrairement aux trois autres options.

Synonyme de « wiped out » : **eliminated** (ou « eradicated », « destroyed »).

### Conseil
Pour une question de synonyme isolée en fin de compréhension, vérifie que le mot proposé garde exactement le même sens dans le contexte précis du texte (ici, l'élimination presque totale d'une maladie), pas seulement un sens proche en général.
